subject: Unified SKU mapping for cross-listing parity & partner payout model
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@datanexus.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. We are starting to map Redwood SKUs into our internal catalog and need two things to move forward with procurement: a cross-listing SKU mapping that preserves list-price parity across AWS/GCP/Azure marketplaces, and a clear partner payout / reseller netback model so our channel team can validate margins.

Attached is a short workbook showing our expected monthly consumption mix (metered vs reserved) and a rough ARR target for year one. Can you provide a proposal that: 
- Shows how you would map a single Redwood offering into the three marketplace SKUs without creating arbitrage opportunities,
- Proposes an initial partner payout schedule (percent or fixed pass-through), and
- Notes invoice routing requirements so we can confirm with finance.

Timing: we are aiming to finalize a private offer by end of November. Appreciate a quick sketch and a sample pricing matrix.

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Lead, DataNexus
[Attachment: DataNexus_PRICING_REQUEST.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Elena,

Thanks for the workbook and clear ask. Quick response with a proposed structure so your team has something to review: 

1) Cross-listing approach (preventing arbitrage)- We recommend a single canonical internal SKU for the Redwood product and three marketplace listing SKUs that are functionally identical but tied to a private-offer price map. The private-offer mapping ensures the same net effective price after marketplace transaction fees.

2) Pricing models to support (we will include an example matrix)- Metered hourly (metered token/execution): list price set at N, marketplace fee transparency included.- Reserved node commitment (monthly node-hour bundle): blended effective $/token after commitment.

3) Partner payout / channel netback (initial suggestion)- Option A (standard): 15% reseller netback on list price (passed through as a separate payout line).- Option B (accelerator): 20% first-year netback if DataNexus commits to 12 months of reserved capacity > 50% of expected ARR.

4) Invoice routing and evidence- We can route invoices through marketplace billing (recommended for visibility) or direct invoicing if you need tightened procurement terms. If routed via marketplace, we require the buyer account linkage and an invoice routing flag in the private offer. For direct invoicing, we'll need the purchase order and billing contact.

I'll attach a draft cross-listing CSV and a sample pricing matrix in the next message. Ben and Laura are looped for commission and finance routing checks. Let us know which option you prefer and we will convert to a private-offer draft.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_cross-listing-matrix_v1.csv (csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Quick notes from GTM/commissions side: 
- If DataNexus wants reseller payouts to show as a separate line item on the marketplace settlement, we can do that for AWS and GCP; Azure has tighter constraints and might require a pass-through invoice.
- For internal forecasting I recommend we treat the netback as a marketing allowance for the first year (accelerator model) so we can protect gross ARR and provide the 20% uplift without impacting quota recognition.
- We should propose a reconciliation cadence (quarterly) and include an evidence bundle for claims.

I'll draft the payout line language and upload to the pricing matrix so Elena can see the netback across scenarios.

Ben
Director, Marketplace GTM

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Elena and team,

A couple of compliance/finance callouts we need to confirm before finalizing: 
- Tax handling: clarify whether reseller netback is treated as a rebate (reduces invoice) or as a separate payout (subject to different tax treatment). This affects how DataNexus reports cost of goods.
- Proof for pass-through: we'll provide monthly usage reports; however, if you route invoices via marketplace, marketplace settlement reports are the canonical source.
- Invoice terms: trade terms will default to 30 days net unless a different term is requested in the PO.

If you want us to run an explicit comparison matrix (list price -> marketplace fees -> netback -> effective price) for the three clouds using your consumption mix, say so and we'll run the numbers for next-day delivery.

Thanks,
Laura
Finance Ops Lead

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@datanexus.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Camila — thanks for the clear options. We prefer Option B (20% first-year netback tied to 12-month reserved commitment), but finance asked for two modifications: 
1) Make the 20% a refundable marketing allowance rather than a gross invoice reduction (keeps our COGS reporting intact).
2) Provide a one-page reconciliation template we can use for monthly settlements.

If you can update the matrix with those two points and give a sample DocuSign-ready private-offer draft, procurement will push to sign by Nov 30.

Elena

(Also looping in AWS Marketplace AM for any constraints on marketplace settlement lines.)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datanexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace AM <aws-am@awsmarketplace.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU parity across marketplaces + partner payout question

Elena — appreciate the direction. Attached is an updated pricing matrix and a one-page reconciliation template. Key points in this draft: 
- We mark the 20% as a marketing allowance (separate payout) and will pay it quarterly against verified usage; this will not reduce invoice amounts.
- Invoice routing: we will default to marketplace routing for AWS/GCP; Azure will be direct invoice with a pass-through line for the allowance.
- Reconciliation template included; we will accept DataNexus monthly usage export + marketplace settlement as primary evidence.
- DocuSign draft: link below. If that looks good we will kick off the private-offer creation: https://www.docusign.com/link/NTY4MjM-Redwood-DNX-PO

Attachments: redwood_cross-listing-matrix_v2.csv, DNX-Reconciliation-template_v1.pdf

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the marketing-allowance approach and we will prepare the private offer (we expect a 48-hour turnaround after confirmation).

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_cross-listing-matrix_v2.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: DNX-Reconciliation-template_v1.pdf (pdf)]
